INTERNATIONAL World Watch By: Agencies Date: July 26, 2026 Share post: WhatsApp Facebook X ReddIt Telegram Linkedin l35 killed in Syria bus collision Damascus, July 25: At least 35 people have been killed and dozens injured after two buses collided on a highway linking the Syrian capital with the eastern province of Deir el-Zour on Saturday, state media reported. Around 30 people were injured in the crash between a civilian bus and an Interior Ministry bus on the desert highway, the SANA news agency cited a health ministry official as saying. Syrian military helicopters were reported to be involved in the operation at the scene. The cause of the collision was not immediately known. (AP) Romania shoots down 2nd drone in two days Bucharest, July 25: Romanian President Nicusor Dan said Saturday that Romania had shot down another drone after it violated the country’s airspace, marking the second such incident in two days. The drone was downed about 10 km west of Sfantu Gheorghe in central Romania, Dan said. Romania’s Ministry of National Defence said in a statement that its radar surveillance systems detected an unauthorised drone entering the eastern European country’s national airspace and flying in the border area with Ukraine, Xinhua News Agency reported. “Two F-16 Fighting Falcon aircraft of the Romanian Air Force intercepted the air target and executed standard identification and neutralisation procedures. The drone was safely shot down in an unpopulated area near the border,” the ministry said. It added that the drone was brought down by the same pilot who had shot down the Shahed drone in Buzau County on Friday. (IANS) Quarter million flee France, Spain wildfires France, July 25: France was preparing to use a massive specially adapted cargo aircraft to dump flame retardants Saturday on a wildfire that has forced the evacuation of tens of thousands of people, including from some suburbs of the wine region city of Bordeaux. Including some 70,000 people evacuated in central Spain, wildfires in southern Europe this week have displaced more than 250,000 people. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the hulking A400M aircraft will join 18 other water- and retardant-dropping planes and helicopters waging an expected “long and very difficult” battle against the blaze raging in the Gironde region of southwestern France. (AP) Okefenokee Swamp added to UNESCO List Seoul, July 25: The Okefenokee Swamp in Georgia, an ornate 13th-century Buddhist temple in Thailand and tidal flats in western South Korea were among several sites added to the World Heritage List on Saturday at a UN committee meeting in South Korea. The UNESCO meetings in Busan, which continue through next Wednesday, are reviewing dozens of other nominations, including the D-Day landing beaches in France, Mount Olympus in Greece and the ancient Japanese capitals of Asuka-Fujiwara.The Okefenokee Swamp is regarded as one of the world’s largest freshwater ecosystems, encompassing a vast network of wetlands that supports exceptional biodiversity and serves as the source of two major rivers. Photograph: Paul Sancya/AP View image in fullscreen Mike Rogers speaks during a campaign event on 20 August 2026 in Detroit. Photograph: Paul Sancya/AP Michigan Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers says he saw Bin Laden’s body with his ‘own eyes’. He did not Ex-House intel committee chair, now running against Abdul El-Sayed, instead saw photo of Osama bin Laden’s body Robert Mackey Sat 29 Aug 2026 11.07 EDT Last modified on Sat 29 Aug 2026 11.09 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google In a recent fundraising email, the Republican candidate for Michigan ’s open US Senate seat, former congressman Mike Rogers, appeared to mislead supporters about his past by suggesting that he had played an active role in the killing of Osama bin Laden , the leader of al-Qaida who was shot and killed in an American military raid on his compound in Pakistan in 2011. “When I served as a US army officer and an FBI special agent, I swore a sacred oath to defend the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic,” Rogers wrote, according to a screenshot of the email shared online by Azi Paybarah, a former Washington Post reporter now with Straight Arrow News. “I dedicated my life to keeping our families safe – working in the shadows, hunting down terrorists, and standing on the frontlines of our national security.” He then added, in a section of the email highlighted in bold type: “I saw the dead body of Osama bin Laden with my own eyes, knowing that together, we had delivered justice for America.” Democrats ignored the uncommitted movement for Gaza in 2024. Now, it’s winning elections Read more Rogers, however, was not in Abbottabad, Pakistan, on 1 May 2011, when Bin Laden was shot and killed – nor was he in the White House Situation Room , where then president Barack Obama and senior administration officials at the time, including Joe Biden and Hillary Clinton, followed the raid in real time. Instead, as Rogers told reporters the next day , and recounts in a campaign video , he was at home in Washington DC – where, as the chair of the House intelligence committee at the time, he was informed about the raid in a phone call from Obama’s CIA director, Leon Panetta. While the Rogers campaign did not respond to requests to explain what the former congressman meant by his claim, Paybarah, who first reported the fundraising email sent by Rogers on Sunday, suggested that Rogers must have been referring to the fact that he was one of a select few US officials to have seen a photograph of Bin Laden’s dead body. Rogers said – days after the raid – that the photograph he’d seen made it clear that Bin Laden was dead. But he said he supported Obama’s decision to not make the graphic images of the raid public. “The risks of release outweigh the benefits,” Rogers said in a statement at the time. “Conspiracy theorists around the world will just claim the photos are doctored anyway, and there is a real risk that releasing the photos will only serve to inflame public opinion in the Middle East.” In the years since, though, Rogers has frequently referred to his role as a congressman who helped provide funds for US intelligence agencies in vague terms that seemed to exaggerate his role. Since Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim doctor and former public health official, became his opponent in the Senate race, Rogers has repeatedly cited his own role in the US war on Islamist terrorism in his campaign statements. “Abdul doesn’t represent a vision for the future. He’s leading a movement grounded in ideological fanaticism,” Rogers said the night that El-Sayed won the Democratic nomination. “I spent years hunting terrorists and bringing Osama bin Laden to justice. Never in a million years did I think that I would be running against someone who believes America deserved 9/11.” A New York Times factcheck pointed out that the second part of Rogers’ “incendiary statement” was false: it was not El-Sayed, but one of his supporters, the Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who once said that American deserved 9/11, before retracting and apologizing for that statement seven years before he endorsed El-Sayed. For his part, El-Sayed has clearly denounced the 9/11 attacks for years. In a recollection of that day written in 2021, El-Sayed wrote : “I watched terrorists with names like mine attack my country in the name of my faith. Three thousand of my fellow Americans were killed in the craven terrorist attacks in New York, Washington DC and Pennsylvania. The attack devastated me.” Explore more on these topics Michigan US Senate Osama bin Laden US midterm elections 2026 Republicans US politics news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

Japan tests mobile robotic rubbish bins at Shinjuku Station Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 18/09/2026 - 16:38 GMT+2 Japan's busiest railway station is testing mobile robotic rubbish bins in Tokyo, with the aim of easing the workload of sanitation workers. … More Three automated bins are being trialled at Shinjuku Station , where more than 2.7 million passengers pass through the wider complex each day. Standing just over one metre tall and moving at a cautious 20 centimetres per second , the machines can stop quickly around passengers. The trial began on 8 September and runs until 20 November on weekdays between 10:00 and 17:00 on the first basement-level paid concourse. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Run by East Japan Railway in the world's busiest rail hub, the project addresses a setting where fixed bins have been reduced for cleanliness and security , and traditional bins are emptied manually more than 10 times a day . The robots follow pre-programmed circular routes between ticket gates to collect general waste and plastic bottles, returning autonomously to a collection point when full. Designed to assist human workers rather than replace them , Japan Railway is assessing commuter engagement and safe navigation through busy underground areas, using video and sensor data solely for analysis. While some passengers have welcomed the concept, tourists have been drawn to the devices' large, googly eyes and train-themed livery featuring the station mascot, Shinjukuma . https://www.dw.com/en/despite-restrictiv.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PR3y Prefer DW on Google Polish activist Justyna Wydrzynska helps to operate the 'Abortomat,' a locker that allows women to access abortion pills swiftly and anonymously Image: Adam Easton/DW Advertisement Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws . Known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk . The Polish prime minister pledged to introduce abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy before the 2023 parliamentary election, but his coalition has been unable to agree on a common position. Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request. In Poland, abortion is only allowed when the pregnancy is the result of a crime — rape or incest — or when it endangers the health or life of the woman. Pink lockers and PIN codes Justyna Wydrzynska , an activist from a nonprofit organization called Abortion Dream Team, showed DW the "Abortomat" in a small room behind a tasseled portiere at Abotak, Poland's first abortion center. Abotak, Poland's first abortion center, is situated opposite the Polish parliament and houses the 'Abortomat' Image: Adam Easton/DW Inside, the pink lighting is subdued. Glitter tassels, baubles and spotlights make it feel a bit like a disco, she said. The "Abortomat," which opened in late September, has 22 pink lockers. To open one, a woman receives a PIN code from the organization Women Help Women after completing a medical questionnaire, which is then checked by a doctor. Parcel lockers have sprung up like mushrooms after rain in Poland in recent years. Even the smallest villages have them. "When you walk around Poland, vending machines are everywhere. This is our culture. People in the US have Amazon, we have vending machines for everything," said Wydrzynska. Convicted of helping a woman to have an abortion Women in Poland who have an abortion are not criminalized. But anyone who helps them terminate a pregnancy risks up to three years in prison. In 2023, Wydrzynska was the first activist to be convicted in Poland of helping a woman to have an abortion by sending her pills. The conviction was later overturned, and the court ordered a retrial. 'Abortomat': World's first abortion pill-dispensing locker in Poland To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Inside each compartment at the "Abortomat" is a package that normally contains two drugs, mifepristone and misoprostol, usually taken up to the 14th week of pregnancy. Because mifepristone is not registered in Poland, the drug must be ordered from abroad where it is legal. Information on how to do this is not easy to come by, which is where Abortion Dream Team and Abotak come in. They help women find information about accessing medication, which is sent from abroad by Women Help Women, or help them to travel abroad for a termination. A 'complicated' legal situation Wydrzynska said she believes the "Abortomat" does not break the law because it is a machine, not a person, that is delivering the pills, although she admits she is not sure. Dr. Sabrina Mana-Walasek, a reproductive rights lawyer representing Wydrzynska, said the legal environment for abortion pills is "complicated." She said that although mifepristone is not registered in Poland, it is registered in the European Union and, as EU citizens, Polish women can order it and take it. "If a woman orders pills for herself and pays for them herself, it's not a crime," she said. Opposition from Catholic groups The ultra-Catholic legal group Ordo Iuris disagrees and has notified the prosecutor's office that the activists are committing a crime. "In the case of an 'Abortomat,' the actions enabling a woman to have an abortion are theoretically performed by the woman herself using the device, but the reality is that this machine is operated by people — they send the code required to open the compartment containing abortion pills, they order and procure the pills, and they restock the compartments," said Katarzyna Gesiak, director of the Ordo Iuris Center for Medical Law and Bioethics. Comforting messages can be seen inside the Abotak center Image: Adam Easton/DW Wydrzynska said anti-abortion activists regularly demonstrate outside Abotak, using horns and loudspeakers to generate loud noise to annoy the center's residential neighbors and pressure the landlord to revoke their rental agreement. At one demonstration, a woman holding an image of the Virgin Mary told DW she believes abortion "is the work of Satan." "Abortion is evil, it's demonic, it's against the fifth Commandment, 'Thou shalt not kill,'" she said. Support for women seeking an abortion Earlier this year, Diana, a 25-year-old Ukrainian woman living in Warsaw , used abortion pills during her sixth week of pregnancy before the "Abortomat" started up. She got the pills using information provided by Abortion Dream Team. Diana told DW that she has never wanted to have children. "I was expecting something like a headache, stomachache, maybe vomiting, but I had nothing like that. It was just like a normal period. I didn't feel any pain. It was really easy for me," she said. "I felt relief because I knew that it was the right choice for me. I knew that I can live my life," she added. Before receiving a PIN code for the locker, a woman first has to complete a medical questionnaire from the organization Women Help Women Image: Adam Easton/DW Another Abortion Dream Team activist, Natalia Broniarczyk, said they help about 130 women daily in Poland. About 125 of these women use pills that cost about €75 ($83), while the remainder travel to a clinic abroad. In contrast, just 851 abortions were performed in Polish hospitals last year. Rising support for right-wing parties Broniarczyk is concerned about the rising support for right-wing parties ahead of next year's parliamentary election, but she's also furious at the inactivity of liberals in Tusk's coalition. "I'm mad at the liberals because for three years, they did nothing to protect us. They lost three years and now, when we're close to an election, they are fighting for our voices and respect. People are more progressive than politicians," she said. After taking office in 2023, Tusk's coalition, which includes left-wing and conservative partners, were unable to agree a common position and their separate bills failed to obtain parliamentary approval in 2024. Natalia Broniarczyk believes Poland's president, Karol Nawrocki, will use his power of veto to block two bills recently passed by the country's parliament that would make abortion more accessible Image: Adam Easton/DW Afterwards, Tusk said abortion on request would not be possible during the current parliamentary term. Two bills approved by parliament In October, however, two bills were resubmitted to the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, and were narrowly approved. One reinstates severe irreversible fetal defects as a justification for a legal termination. This justification had been ruled illegal by the Constitutional Court in 2020 when the previous right-wing Law and Justice (PiS) -led government was in power. The 2020 ruling led to tens of thousands of people, mostly women, taking part in street protests in towns and cities across the country, some of the largest since communism fell in 1989. Lawmakers also approved a bill partially decriminalizing anyone who helps a woman terminate her pregnancy. According to the results of a recent poll conducted by SW Research for Onet.pl , almost 61% of respondents said they want the country's right-wing president, Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, to sign into law the bill on the fetal defect justification. Nawrocki opposes abortion, and both Wydrzynska and Broniarczyk think he will use his power of veto to block the bills, preventing them from becoming law.
